title: Hamzah and Umar
year: Dhul-Hijjah, the sixth year of prophethood — c. 616 CE
teaser: Three days apart, two of the most feared men in Makkah joined. After that the Muslims prayed at the Ka'bah.

layers.title: Two Names in One Month
layers.subtitle: What the community looked like before them
layers.content:
By the sixth year of prophethood the Muslims in Makkah were a diminished and careful body. The best of the vulnerable had gone across the sea. Those who stayed were either notables safe by their own standing, neighbours of such men, or people keeping their belief as quiet as they could manage. They met at the house of al-Arqam on as-Safa, and they prayed inside four walls.

Against that, one prayer is recorded. At-Tirmidhi preserves it: 'O Allah, give strength to Islam through whichever of these two men You love more — Umar ibn al-Khattab, or Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.'

Read the pairing. He asked for one of the two hardest men in the city, and named the architect of the torture campaign as an acceptable answer. Neither was a likely convert. Umar regarded the traditions of his people highly, drank with his circle, and had handled Muslim women himself, before his conversion, in the persecutions.

The other man was the Prophet's own uncle. Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, whose kunyah was Abu Umarah, was a hunter and a fighter with standing in Bani Hashim, and up to that point he had not taken a position. Ibn Sa'd, who names him the Lion of Allah and Lion of His Messenger, dates his entry to after the Prophet ﷺ had moved to the house of al-Arqam, in the sixth year.

In one month of Dhul-Hijjah, three days apart, both men came in. Nothing about the message changed. What changed was who was standing behind it.
layers.hadith_ref: The du'a for Umar or Abu Jahl — at-Tirmidhi, Chapters of Virtues, the virtue of Umar ibn al-Khattab
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat al-Kubra, Vol. III; Tarikh Umar ibn al-Khattab by Ibn al-Jawzi — in Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Hunter Comes Back
layers.subtitle: A bow across the shoulder, and a bleeding head
layers.content:
Ibn Hisham gives it this way. The Prophet ﷺ was sitting on the hillock of as-Safa when Abu Jahl passed and began abusing the religion he preached. The Prophet ﷺ said nothing. Abu Jahl went on unchecked, then picked up a stone and struck his head with it until it bled. Then he walked off to join the Quraysh in their assembly.

Shortly afterwards Hamzah came back along the same road from a hunting expedition, his bow slung on his shoulder. A slave-girl belonging to Abdullah ibn Jad'an had watched the whole thing, and she told him what had been done.

Hamzah went to the Ka'bah. He found Abu Jahl in the courtyard of the sanctuary sitting with a company of Quraysh, walked up to him, and brought the bow down on his head hard enough to split it open. Then he said it in front of all of them: you have been abusing Muhammad — I follow his religion, and I say what he says.

The men of Bani Makhzum moved to defend Abu Jahl. The men of Bani Hashim moved to back Hamzah. It was Abu Jahl who stopped it: leave Abu Umarah alone — by Allah, I did shamelessly abuse his nephew.

Ibn Sa'd records the same conversion with different particulars: that Abu Jahl together with Adi ibn al-Hamra' and Ibn al-Asda' attacked and insulted the Prophet ﷺ, that Hamzah heard of it, entered the sanctuary in anger and cut Abu Jahl's head open, and became Muslim, and that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was made strong through him. The reports differ on the details of the provocation. They agree on the bow, the head, and the declaration.

Al-Mubarakpuri is careful about the motive. Hamzah moved first as a man who would not have his relative humiliated. That is where it started. Afterwards, he writes, Allah purified his nature and he took hold of the most trustworthy handhold, and became a source of great strength to the faith.
layers.source: Ibn Hisham 1/291-292; Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat al-Kubra, Vol. III — in Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Man With the Sword
layers.subtitle: He set out to kill him and was turned aside by a page
layers.content:
Umar's turning happened in stages, and he was fighting it the whole way.

He came to the sanctuary one day and found the Prophet ﷺ praying, reciting the opening of Surah al-Haqqah. He said to himself: this is poetry, exactly as Quraysh have said. The recitation continued: 'It is not the word of a poet — little is that you believe.' He thought: then he is a soothsayer. The recitation continued: 'Nor is it the word of a soothsayer — little is that you remember. This is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds.' Umar's own words about that moment: 'Then Islam came into my heart.'

He went on persecuting anyway. Some time later he left his house with his sword, intending to kill the Prophet ﷺ. A man met him on the way — the sources name Nu'aym ibn Abdullah, or a man of Zahrah, or one of Makhzum — asked where he was going, and told him to look to his own household first: his sister and her husband had left his religion.

He went to his sister's house. From outside he heard Khabbab ibn al-Aratt reciting Surah Ta-Ha from a page. Khabbab went inside; Fatimah hid the page. Umar came in demanding to know what he had heard, struck his brother-in-law, and when his sister moved to shield her husband, struck her on the head. Both of them told him then: yes, we are Muslims, we believe in Allah and His Messenger, so do what you will.

He saw his sister's face smeared with blood, and something gave way. Let me see what you were reading. She made him wash first — none but the pure may touch it. He washed, took the page, and read until: «إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي» — 'Verily I am Allah; there is no god but I, so worship Me and maintain the prayer for My remembrance.' (20:14) He said: how excellent this is, and how graceful. Take me to Muhammad.

At that Khabbab came out of hiding and told him about the du'a.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 20:14 — the verse Umar read on his sister's page
layers.source: Tarikh Umar ibn al-Khattab pp. 6-11; Ibn Hisham 1/343-347 — in Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: The Door at as-Safa
layers.subtitle: No verse came down — the verses were already there
layers.content:
He walked to the house at as-Safa with the sword still swinging at his arm and knocked. One of the Companions looked through a crack in the door and turned back worried: it is Umar, with his sword. It was Hamzah, three days a Muslim, who settled the room: let him in — as a friend he is welcome, and as an enemy he will have his head cut off with his own sword.

The Prophet ﷺ told them to open it. He came forward to meet the man, took hold of his garment and his scabbard, and asked him why he had come. Umar said: O Messenger of Allah, I come to believe in Allah and in His Messenger and in what he has brought from his Lord. Al-Mubarakpuri records that the takbir the household raised was loud enough to be heard at the Ka'bah.

No revelation is recorded as having come down about either of these two conversions. What the sources record instead is which verses did the work, and both times the verse answered a specific objection.

For Umar it was Surah al-Haqqah, refusing his two theories in the order he produced them: not the word of a poet (69:41), not the word of a soothsayer (69:42), but a revelation from the Lord of the worlds (69:43). He was not persuaded by an argument. He was answered mid-thought, twice.

Then Ta-Ha, which does not argue at all: I am Allah, there is no god but I, so worship Me and keep up the prayer for My remembrance. (20:14) A page in his sister's house, a command with no premise attached.

His first act as a Muslim was to knock on Abu Jahl's door and say it to his face; the door was slammed on him. When Quraysh gathered in the valley to kill him, it was al-As ibn Wa'il as-Sahmi — no Muslim, but an old ally of his family — who told them there was no way anybody would touch the man, and the crowd went home. al-Bukhari records it from Abdullah ibn Umar.
layers.quran_ref: Quran 69:40-43 — 'It is not the word of a poet... nor the word of a soothsayer... this is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds'
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar — al-As ibn Wa'il's protection of Umar
layers.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 1/545; Ibn Hisham 1/349; Tarikh Umar ibn al-Khattab pp. 7-11 — in Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar

layers.title: What It Left Behind
layers.subtitle: They walked to the sanctuary in two columns
layers.content:
Umar did not stay quiet about the arrangement he had joined. Ibn Abbas reports, through Mujahid, what he asked the Prophet ﷺ: are we not on the right path, here and in the Hereafter? He was told: of course you are. Then why do we conduct ourselves in secret? By Allah, we will leave our concealment and proclaim this openly.

They went out in two groups in broad daylight, Hamzah leading one and Umar the other, and walked to the sanctuary. Al-Mubarakpuri records what happened to the faces of the polytheists who watched them arrive. It was on that occasion that the Prophet ﷺ gave Umar the name al-Farooq — the one who separates truth from falsehood.

The Companions' own testimony is blunt about what these two conversions bought. Ibn Mas'ud: we were never able to pray at the Ka'bah until Umar accepted Islam. Suhayb ibn Sinan ar-Rumi: only after Umar's conversion did they proclaim the call, gather, and circle the Sacred House freely, and even dare to answer back some of the wrongs done to them. Ibn Mas'ud again, in al-Bukhari: we were greatly strengthened when Umar accepted Islam.

The reaction on the other side was strategic. Quraysh concluded that torture was no longer producing results, and switched to a different instrument — money, rank and the offer of kingship, which is where the negotiations belong.

One thing to carry, and it is uncomfortable. Hamzah entered Islam in a temper, over an insult to a relative, and the sirah says so without embarrassment. Umar entered it after hearing the truth clearly, refusing it, persecuting people for months, then striking his own sister in the head. Neither man came in clean. Both were used. Whatever a person's route in was, it is what happens afterwards that the sources troubled to write down.
layers.hadith_ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 1/545 — Ibn Mas'ud: 'We were greatly strengthened when Umar accepted Islam'
layers.source: Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar (Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum), Darussalam

quiz.prompt: In the du'a recorded by at-Tirmidhi, which two men did the Prophet ﷺ name when asking Allah to strengthen Islam?

options.text: Abu Talib or al-Abbas
Umar ibn al-Khattab or Abu Jahl ibn Hisham
Hamzah or Abu Lahab
Utbah ibn Rabi'ah or Umayyah ibn Khalaf

quiz.citation: at-Tirmidhi, Chapters of Virtues — the virtue of Umar ibn al-Khattab
quiz.scholar_reflection: He asked for whichever of the two Allah loved more, and one of the two named was the man who had authorised the torture campaign. Umar was the one who received it.

quiz.prompt: What triggered Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib's conversion, according to Ibn Hisham?

options.text: A dream he had while travelling to Syria
Hearing that Abu Jahl had struck the Prophet's head with a stone at as-Safa
The recitation of Surah an-Najm in the sanctuary
A request from Abu Talib to protect his nephew

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/291-292 — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: A slave-girl of Abdullah ibn Jad'an had seen it and told him as he came back from hunting. Ibn Sa'd records the provocation differently; the reports agree on what Hamzah then did with his bow.

quiz.prompt: Which surah was Umar reciting from his sister's page when he said 'take me to Muhammad'?

options.text: Surah Ta-Ha
Surah Maryam
Surah al-Masad
Surah al-Fatihah

quiz.citation: Quran 20:14 — Tarikh Umar ibn al-Khattab pp. 6-11; Ibn Hisham 1/343-347
quiz.scholar_reflection: He had to wash before she would let him hold it. He read as far as: I am Allah, there is no god but I, so worship Me and keep up the prayer for My remembrance.

quiz.prompt: Who told the Companions to open the door when Umar arrived at the house on as-Safa with his sword?

options.text: Abu Bakr
Ali ibn Abi Talib
Hamzah, three days a Muslim himself
Khabbab ibn al-Aratt

quiz.citation: Tarikh Umar ibn al-Khattab pp. 7-11; Ibn Hisham 1/343-346
quiz.scholar_reflection: 'As a friend he is welcome. As a foe, he will have his head cut off with his own sword.' The first conversion made the second one possible to receive.

quiz.prompt: What did the Companions say changed after Umar's conversion?

options.text: Quraysh lifted the boycott of Bani Hashim
The emigrants returned from Abyssinia for good
They were able to pray at the Ka'bah, which they had not been able to do before
Abu Talib publicly accepted Islam

quiz.citation: Sahih al-Bukhari 1/545, narrated by Ibn Mas'ud
quiz.scholar_reflection: Ibn Mas'ud: we were never able to pray at the Ka'bah until Umar accepted Islam. Suhayb ar-Rumi adds that only then did they circle the Sacred House freely.

quiz.prompt: Al-Mubarakpuri says Hamzah's conversion began in the pride of a man who would not have his relative humiliated, and that his nature was purified afterwards. How do you read a beginning like that?

options.text: Allah uses the motive a person actually has, not the one they should have had
The declaration was still a declaration — he said it in front of the whole assembly
It is honest of the sources to say it, and that honesty is worth more than a tidy story
Intentions can be corrected after the fact; entry is not the same as arrival

quiz.citation: Ibn Hisham 1/291-292 — Al-Mubarakpuri, The Sealed Nectar
quiz.scholar_reflection: He struck a man over an insult, and ended as the Lion of Allah. The sirah does not hide the first fact in order to protect the second.

quiz.prompt: Umar heard Surah al-Haqqah answer both of his objections in sequence, said 'then Islam came into my heart' — and then went on persecuting Muslims for a while longer. What does that gap tell you?

options.text: Being convinced and being willing to act are two different events
Pride and inherited loyalty can hold a person in place long after they know better
It makes his eventual submission heavier, because it cost him more
Most people are somewhere in that gap about something, right now

quiz.citation: Quran 69:40-43 — Tarikh Umar ibn al-Khattab p. 6
quiz.scholar_reflection: The verses had already answered him. What remained was not information. It was the cost of acting on it in front of his own people.

quiz.prompt: He struck his sister on the head, saw the blood on her face, and asked to read the page. What do you take from that turn?

options.text: Seeing the cost of his own violence in front of him broke something loose
Their answer under the blows — do what you will, we are Muslims — was the argument he could not beat
She still made him wash before touching it; she did not soften on the thing that mattered
He wanted to know what could make his sister accept that, and curiosity was the opening

quiz.citation: Tarikh Umar ibn al-Khattab pp. 6-11; Ibn Hisham 1/343-347
quiz.scholar_reflection: Bleeding, she refused to hand him the page until he had washed. The line she held is part of why he crossed it.

quiz.prompt: When Quraysh gathered to kill Umar, the man who protected him was al-As ibn Wa'il — not a Muslim, but an old ally of his family. What do you make of that?

options.text: The tribal system that crushed the weak also shielded the well-connected, and that is the whole point
Allah's protection arrives through ordinary means, including people who do not believe
Umar was saved by exactly what Bilal and Sumayyah did not have
Obligations of loyalty can outlast disagreement about the deepest things

quiz.citation: Sahih al-Bukhari 1/545, narrated by Abdullah ibn Umar
quiz.scholar_reflection: One sentence from a man of standing sent the whole valley home. The same crowd had had no reason to stop over a slave.

quiz.prompt: After these two conversions Quraysh stopped relying on torture and began offering wealth, rank and kingship instead. Which of the two do you consider the more dangerous instrument?

options.text: Bribery — it does not create martyrs, and it works on people who would not break under pain
Torture — nothing tests a person like the body being used against them
The switch is what matters: they moved to whichever tool the community was weakest against
Comfort is harder to resist than pain because it never announces itself as an attack

quiz.scholar_reflection: They only offered money after the beatings stopped working. The change in method is a reading of the community's new strength.
